items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: I was writing about the Miles Davis Sextet and trying to ask the question how did these people go about improvising

ctx.x: Yeah. A student of mine just sent me a wonderful album of a singer/trumpet player from Spain I think, Andrea Motis. And she did this, I know, me neither. And she did those songs like, oh God, and she copped the arrangements and the whole thing and I was so happy to hear it. I’m also, I can’t get away from Cannonball for a minute, because he’s like my musical hero. And when you approached in your book Twilight of Bebop, can you talk about Cannonball for a minute? That’s a way open ended question.

Yeah, that’s a long time ago. That was my Ph.D. dissertation, that’s what got me into this writing about jazz in a scholarly way. And I was writing about the Miles Davis Sextet and trying to ask the question how did these people go about improvising and see if it © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

could be analyzed in some sort of useful way, which is all an introduction to say that I actually don’t love his playing as much as I used to. I love his ballad playing but his beboppy stuff is too many notes and not enough space for my taste.
